selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of power is needed for even one apple to be prepared and given as food to a person?
questions.answer: It requires the power of the One Who controls the large movements of the world, like the cycle of time and the turning of the earth.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the source of true provision?
questions.answer: True provision comes from the Creator Who manages the whole world.

questions.question: How does the passage help us see a connection between food and the universe?
questions.answer: It teaches that the food we receive comes through the ordered working of the whole cosmos.

questions.question: What can we infer from the same marks appearing on many different living things?
questions.answer: They all come from the same Creator, not from many separate makers.

questions.question: Why does the passage say those same signs appear on many other created things too?
questions.answer: To show unity in creation and that all are made by the same Maker.

questions.question: How is the apple related to other beings in the world in this passage?
questions.answer: It is described as belonging among similar and related creatures under one Lord.

questions.question: What is meant by calling the universe the apple’s tree or factory?
questions.answer: It means the apple is produced through the working of the whole creation, not by itself.

questions.question: What is the purpose of saying that every fruit is like a stamp?
questions.answer: The purpose is to show that each fruit carries proof of one Creator.

questions.question: How does the number of fruits strengthen the proof mentioned at the end?
questions.answer: Every fruit adds another witness to the same truth, so the evidence becomes very great.

questions.question: What is the central claim made about a single apple in the passage?
questions.answer: A single apple can only be made and given by the Creator Who rules over the whole universe.

questions.question: Why does the passage describe the earth with an image of transport and delivery?
questions.answer: To show that provision is brought to people through a planned system.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by mentioning days, nights, and seasons together?
questions.answer: It suggests a complete, balanced order that serves the coming of provision.

questions.question: Why can the apple not be understood as something made in isolation?
questions.answer: Because its existence depends on many connected causes and conditions in creation.

questions.question: What is the logical link between the apple and the rest of the natural world?
questions.answer: The apple is part of an interconnected creation, so its maker must have authority over that whole network.

questions.question: Why must the maker of the apple also be the maker of the cosmos in this argument?
questions.answer: Because the cosmos functions like the larger setting and producing system needed for the apple.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the earth, the cosmos, the seasons, and warm months together?
questions.answer: To show that the fruit is connected to a complete system of place, process, and timing.

questions.question: According to the final lines, what does each fruit make known?
questions.answer: Each fruit makes known the One Who created the earth and the universe.

questions.question: What does the fruit reveal about the earth and the universe besides providing food?
questions.answer: It reveals that both are meaningful creations made by one wise Lord.

questions.question: In this passage, why is one apple important beyond being something to eat?
questions.answer: It is important because it serves as evidence of Allah’s power, wisdom, and oneness.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak about the turning of the globe?
questions.answer: To show that even one fruit depends on the control of huge realities in creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say is found on the apple and also on other fruits, plants, and animals?
questions.answer: It says the same signs of wise making, mercy, and a mark showing one Maker are found on all of them.

questions.question: What kinds of signs are said to appear on the apple?
questions.answer: Signs of wise design, mercy, and a mark that points to one Lord.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about separate causes making separate things?
questions.answer: It rejects that idea by showing that one fruit is linked to the whole creation.

questions.question: What is meant by calling the world the apple’s garden?
questions.answer: It means the apple grows within the wide place prepared for it by Allah.
